sentences.text: This predator measured between 1.8 and 3.5 meters in length and had a mass of 75 kilograms.
Neuquenraptor possessed a slender, graceful body, long limbs, a curved skull, and sharp claws and teeth.
Although its full appearance is unknown, the fossil shows characteristic crescent-shaped claws.
Its size was similar to Velociraptor, and it likely sported feathers like that species.
Remains were found near Plaza Huincul in the Sierra del Portezuelo in January 1996.
Fernando Novas and Diego Pol formally named and described Neuquenraptor argentinus as a dromaeosaurid in 2005.
The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH 77 comes from layers of the Portezuelo Formation dating to the Coniacian.
Before this find, all dromaeosaurids were known from the Northern Hemisphere, leading scientists to believe the group only inhabited Laurasia.
The discovery of Neuquenraptor provides possible evidence regarding the degree of isolation between the Northern and Southern hemispheres during the Mesozoic.
It is debated whether Neuquenraptor is a junior subjective synonym of Unenlagia, as the latter name was published earlier in 1997 and has priority.
Neuquenraptor lived from the Turonian to the Coniacian, approximately 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
Researchers have attempted to synonymize Neuquenraptor with Unenlagia, but some published analyses suggest Unenlagia is more basal.
